# WSC golden ScriptContexts

**REGENERATED by task N2 against wsc-poc `main` @ `2306678`** (PR #112, "Seize
path: per-pair value delta via CIP-153 builtins, witnessed base delegation").
This is NOT a re-dump of the same bytes: #112 changed two redeemer TYPES and the
fixture identities are now derived from really-compiled scripts, so `paramsHex`,
`redeemerHex` and `scriptContextHex` moved on **all 13** goldens. The pre-#112
JSONs and applied flats are preserved verbatim under `pre-112/` (and the
pre-builder-fix generation before that under `pre-fix/`); both are deliberately
in subdirectories, because `WSC/Goldens/gen-vectors.py` globs
`WSC/goldens/*.json` and asserts exactly 13.

**All 13 still verify** by executing the actual prod-exported script at PV11 —
9 accepting (`Right budget`), 4 rejecting (`Left CekError`). No scenario had to
be dropped or weakened.

## What PR #112 changed in these vectors

| | change | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **base redeemer** | was PlutusTx `()` (`d87980`); now `BaseSpendRedeemer` (`ProgrammableLogicBase.hs:704-709`, `SpendViaGlobal = 0`, `SpendViaSeize = 1`), carrying an INDEX into the credential-sorted withdrawal map | both base goldens now carry `d8799f00ff` = `SpendViaGlobal 0` |
| **global redeemer** | `TransferAct` gained a THIRD field `plgrOwnerWdrlIdxs :: [Integer]` (`:1046-1052`); five fields, not four | `d8799f9f01ff9f01ff8000ff` → `d8799f9f01ff9f01ff808000ff` |
| **seize redeemer** | unchanged wire form | seize `redeemerHex` byte-identical across the change |
| **minting redeemer** | type unchanged, VALUES moved: `BurnOnly 2 → BurnOnly 1`, `DelegateTransfer 2 0 1 0 → 1 0 1 0` | the catalogue now DERIVES these with `withdrawalIndexOf` from derived script hashes, which sort differently from the old synthetic placeholders |
| **script parameters** | `globalCred`, `seizeCred`, `protocolParamsCS` moved from synthetic constants in `ScriptFixtureIds` to values DERIVED from the compiled scripts in `BenchmarkOnchain.PlutarchFixtureIds` | `paramsHex` moved on all 13; the protocol-params datum's `globalLogicCred`/`seizeLogicCred` are still EXACTLY the base validator's two parameters (gated by `RedeemerGate.params_datum_matches_base_script_parameters`) |
| **proof indices** | `transfer-mixed-many-policies` proofs `[1,2,3,4,1] → [1,2,3,1,4]` | `transferProofsFor` sorts by CURRENCY SYMBOL, and the derived symbols permute the sort |

Every index in every redeemer is **computed, never hand-written** — the
catalogue derives them (`withdrawalIndexOf`, `transferProofsFor`,
`seizeIssuerWdrlIdx`, `baseViaGlobalIn`/`baseViaSeizeIn`,
`BenchmarkOnchainScripts.hs:180-244`). This matters because these are
self-validating hints: a wrong index makes the validator REJECT, which would
silently turn an accepting golden into a rejecting one. The `accepts: true` gate
below is what catches that, and all 9 accepting goldens pass it.

**Ledger-shape invariants confirmed present in `main`** (they were added in an
earlier campaign and the task asked whether they survived — they did): the
catalogue builds every context through
`ProgrammableTokens.Test.ScriptContext.Builder.buildLedgerShapedScriptContext`,
giving a positive balanced `txInfoFee`, `txInfoWdrl` (and the matching
`Rewarding` redeemer entries) in `cardano-ledger`'s own `Credential` order, and
min-UTxO ada on every output. Measured consequence: **10 of 13 satisfy CLAB's
`validXContext`** (up from 8 pre-#112), and — the number that actually matters —
**all 9 ACCEPTING goldens satisfy it**. The 3 remaining failures are the
tamper-intrinsic rejecting ones (`WSC/Goldens/Audit.lean`, which builds green
against these vectors without modification).

## Verification method (per golden) — unchanged

1. Read `generated/scripts/unapplied/prod/<validator>.json`, take `cborHex`,
   hex-decode, strip the outer CBOR bytestring wrapper (TextEnvelope double-CBOR,
   same layering `WSC/Imports.lean` handles with `double_cbor_hex`) →
   `SerialisedScript`.
2. Apply the script parameters as `Data` constants with Plutarch's
   `applyArguments` (UPLC `Apply` nodes), reserialise, then
   `PlutusLedgerApi.V3.deserialiseScript vanRossemPV`.
3. `PlutusLedgerApi.V3.evaluateScriptCounting vanRossemPV Verbose evalCtx sfe
   (toData ctx)`, evaluation context from
   `PlutusLedgerApi.Test.V3.EvaluationContext.costModelParamsForTesting`
   (plutus-ledger-api 1.63.0.0 testlib default cost model — indicative of, but
   not identical to, whatever params mainnet publishes for PV11).
4. Gate: `Right budget` required for `accepts: true`, `Left CekError` required
   for `accepts: false`. The rejecting controls double as arity proof: an
   under-applied script can never produce `Left` (it evaluates to a lambda), so
   `Right` on the accepting sibling is not vacuous.

## File format

`{validator, scenario, accepts, paramsHex, redeemerHex, scriptContextHex,
exBudgetCpu, exBudgetMem, sourceTest}` — all hex fields are `serialiseData`
output (CBOR of the `Data`), i.e. exactly the bytes the ledger/CEK sees.
`paramsHex` is in application order. `redeemerHex` duplicates
`scriptContextRedeemer` inside the ctx, exposed separately for the E8
round-trip gates. `exBudgetCpu/Mem` are `null` for rejecting goldens (counting
evaluation aborts).

## Lean bridge

`WSC/Goldens/gen-vectors.py` regenerates `Vectors.lean`, `Terms.lean` and
`TermsCheck.lean` from these JSONs; `--check` verifies committed == generated.
Post-N2 state:

```
CHECK OK: Vectors.lean matches all 13 golden JSONs
CHECK OK: Terms.lean matches all 13 golden JSONs
CHECK OK: TermsCheck.lean matches all 13 golden JSONs
```

`WSC/Goldens/RedeemerGate.lean` was REWRITTEN for the new redeemer shapes. It
gates the mirrors in `WSC/Redeemer.lean` — which task N1 re-cut against 2306678
in the same campaign (`BaseSpendRedeemer` at :99-111, five-field
`PLGRedeemer.TransferAct` at :205-219) — and deliberately does NOT define local
copies of them: a gate over its own instances would prove those instances
correct and say nothing about the ones the library's redeemer-conditioned
theorems actually read. Two clauses are stated at the raw `Data` level so they
survive any future mirror drift: `base_redeemers_are_not_unit` (the base
redeemer is `Constr 0 [I 0]`, not `Constr 0 []`) and
`transfer_goldens_carry_five_fields`.

The three generated files (`Vectors.lean`, `Terms.lean`, `TermsCheck.lean`) now
carry a provenance banner EMITTED BY the generator. Task N1 had hand-added a
"PRE-#112 SUPERSEDED" line to each, which was correct at the time but broke
`--check` (a hand edit to a generated file makes committed != generated). Moving
the banner into `gen-vectors.py` keeps it accurate, survives regeneration, and
restores the gate.

Two NEW coverage gaps opened by #112 are stated in that module rather than
papered over: no golden exercises `BaseSpendRedeemer.SpendViaSeize` (tag 1), and
no golden has a NON-EMPTY `ownerWdrlIdxs` (all four transfer goldens spend
pubkey-stake-owned base inputs, and only script-owned inputs contribute an
entry). The field's POSITION is pinned by
`transfer_field_order_is_discriminating`; its CONTENT is not pinned by any
golden.

## `applied/` — fully applied programs

`applied/<golden>.flat` is the same double-CBOR-hex TextEnvelope layering as
`WSC/flats/*.flat`, but with the script parameters AND the golden
`ScriptContext` already applied as `Data` constants via Plutarch
`applyArguments` — CLOSED, zero-argument programs that start the exact
computation the ledger ran.

Re-verified by `KVerify.lean.disabled` + `verify-applied.py`:
`ALL-MATCH (of 10 decodable; 3 BLOCKED)`. For each of the 10, the `Apply`
spine after the script's own top-level `Force`/let application carries exactly
`paramsHex… ++ [scriptContextHex]`, byte-identical after re-serialisation with
PCB's `PlutusCore.Cbor.encodeData`. None is a bare top-level lambda, so no
measurement is arity-vacuous. The 3 seize flats are BLOCKED for the reason above
— they are WRITTEN and are ledger-deserialisable at PV11 (the golden driver
round-trips each one through the written file and re-runs it), they simply
cannot be read by PCB.
